lib/postgres-spine.js.reason: mergeEventRows fix for a silent data-loss bug (distinct rows sharing a null/duplicate event_seq collapsed onto the same dedup key). The fix needs a two-key (event_seq, event_id) comparator, which Biome's cognitive-complexity scoring counts as added mass even when extracted into its own named function (compareEventRowOrder) — tried extraction first; it did not reduce the file-level score. Correctness over a lower number here.

lib/spine.ts.reason: loadEventsForSummaries batches the summary-hydration N+1 (one query per correlation id -> one query for the whole page) via a ROW_NUMBER()-partitioned fetch plus a per-id grouping pass (building the id->rows Map, iterating placeholders, hydrating rows). That control flow — not the SQL string literal itself — is what Biome's cognitive-complexity scoring counts as added mass; the SQL text's explicit `(event_seq IS NULL), event_seq, event_id` ordering is necessary because summarizeEvents derives status/source/browser-surface state from array position (first/last event, reverse scans), so the grouped rows must arrive in a caller-guaranteed total order rather than relying on the window function's undocumented partition-membership-only guarantee. This mass was already present at PR #368's head without a justification entry; adding one here rather than reducing it further, since the batching mechanism and its ordering contract are load-bearing correctness, not incidental style.

server/connector-manifest-validation.ts.reason: Port of main's external-tool detection hardening (security fix e6e96933b) + owner-cancel/recovery surfaces from #199/#190 reconciliation; behavior required by main's test contract. Queued for decomposition in the Phase-1 drain.

server/db.js.reason: The SQLite migration must inventory recognized enum shapes, preserve dependent objects, rebuild atomically, and fail closed before committing a foreign_key_check. These independent persistence safety branches are necessary to avoid lossy migration of historical schemas.

server/postgres-storage.js.reason: The PostgreSQL migration serializes public legacy bootstraps before catalog discovery with bounded pg_try_advisory_lock polling, distinguishes exact direct legacy/current checks from unrelated compound checks, and performs transactional rollback. The polling/lock classification and fail-closed branches are required to avoid broad constraint deletion, concurrent startup failure, or concurrent-index deadlock.

server/stores/connector-detail-gap-store.reason: The SQLite and Postgres implementations must each make the same run-and-lease-owned compare-and-set transitions for claim, explicit attempt, recovery, re-deferral, release, and expired-lease reclaim. The branches preserve the distinction between an untouched issuance and a real provider attempt across durable backend dialects; collapsing them behind a shallow helper would hide the SQL ownership predicates that prevent re-serve races.

server/routes/ref-device-exporters.ts.reason: decouple-device-enrollment-from-ingest-writer-admission adds the idempotent re-enroll path (handleIdempotentReEnroll) that recovers a one-time device credential lost to a transport failure: it must enforce four independent safeguards (unexpired code, same bound device, device-not-revoked, same binding) before atomically rotating the credential, emit an audit receipt, and reject every other consumed-code replay — plus a typed-503 backpressure mapping (respondEnrollError). The enroll handler itself was decomposed first (performFirstEnrollment, handleIdempotentReEnroll, respondEnrollError all extracted, each within the per-function complexity budget); the residual file-level mass is the four safeguard branches, which are load-bearing correctness for a live credential-loss fix, not incidental style.

server/stores/device-exporter-store.ts.reason: decouple-device-enrollment-from-ingest-writer-admission adds rotateDeviceCredential to both the SQLite and Postgres store backends (the store is a two-backend union, so a new durable primitive necessarily lands twice). Each revokes all non-revoked credentials for the device and inserts exactly one fresh credential; the Postgres variant wraps revoke+insert in withPostgresTransaction so concurrent rotations serialize on the revoke's row locks and exactly one active credential remains. This is the minimum surface for the credential-rotation guarantee and cannot be reduced without dropping one backend.
